title: Awesome journaling app!
content:
I downloaded the app quite a while ago now but I recently started using it daily and I haven’t broken my streak yet.

I am someone who has a lot of thoughts, feelings and emotions on a daily basis.

 so I was motivated to get back into the habit of journaling so that I can have a more consistent log to look back on in the future and/or a place where I may be able to look out for things like emotional patterns around certain events for example.

I would recommend this app to anyone who I  think would benefit from it.

 but I want to especially recommend it to anyone who struggles to write by hand like myself.

The app is really easy to navigate and use which I know can be a major plus to those of us with dexterity issues.

The main features of the app are included in the free version of the app which is also a big plus for anybody!

There is a premium version available that comes with some additional features such as the ability to add audio to your journal entries along with the ability to add multiple photos to one entry instead of just one per entry in the free version.

In my opinion the above features aren’t essential to getting the best out of the app.

 But of course every user has their own opinion on what’s essential for them to be able to journal effectively.

I’ve tried “fancier” journaling apps because of appealing adverts on social media etc but trust me those apps aren’t necessarily as easy to use as this one. 

Also with other apps you need to upgrade to premium in order to use essential features in my opinion.

In this case I think simple is best.

Keep up the good work Day One team! 😊

title: Good app but in desperate need for a design refresh
content:
Overall I’m having a good experience with the app which offers a decent suite of convenient features that give more context to journaling.

My gripe is more with the design. It’s feeling very dated and there are some choices that are really poorly thought through in today’s world. 

For example, there are custom colour themes that apply to a few assets, including text headers, but the same colours are used for both dark and light mode. In practice that means most colours aren’t accessible on their closest theme. Charcoal on dark mode is barely readable. This is just one refinement out of many that are needed.

As mentioned, Day One has the most comprehensive feature set out of the Journal apps, but there are much more elegant ones catching up. I’ve just renewed for another year, but unless there is a decent upgrade to design and performance, it could very well be my last.

title: Good app but in desperate need for a design refresh
content:
Overall I’m having a good experience with the app which offers a decent suite of convenient features that give more context to journaling.

My gripe is more with the design. It’s feeling very dated and there are some choices that are really poorly thought through in today’s world. 

For example, there are custom colour themes that apply to a few assets, including text headers, but the same colours are used for both dark and light mode. In practice that means most colours aren’t accessible on their closest theme. Charcoal on dark mode is barely readable. This is just one refinement out of many that are needed.

As mentioned, Day One has the most comprehensive feature set out of the Journal apps, but there are much more elegant ones catching up. I’ve just renewed for another year, but unless there is a decent upgrade to design and performance, it could very well be my last.

title: Rip off!
content:
Update- exported all my data and moved it to Dairo which does everything I need for a small one off payment. Goodbye DayOne!

I invested in DayOne a year or so ago and bought both the iPhone and Mac apps for a cost of close to £50. I thought it was worth it as a long term investment in my memories and the company had won awards for their apps. So whilst expensive it seemed a worthwhile expense. I was angry when they then decided to bring out DayOne 2 which was a completely new app. I realised that the system I had invested in was no longer going to be developed and so I bought the new iPhone app and transferred my memories to that. I didn't bother with the Mac app as it was far too expensive and I had already paid once and was not paying again after only a few months of use. Now they have done it again - by bringing out a premium subscription I won't benefit from any development. I will not pay any more but will continue to use the version of DayOne I currently have until I find another alternative.  However, I would advise against using DayOne as a first time customer as they lock you in and then start finding ways of charging you more!

title: Some issues
content:
Finally upgraded from the classic version. Some good points - iPhone 11 support, nicer UI - but other parts have gone backwards.

Tags are harder to search and can’t be sorted alphabetically so aren’t as effective to use. I was hoping I’d be able to filter by multiple tags at once.

The calendar view is also quite poor as you no longer get a preview of each entry and a pop-up appears instead, so you can’t quickly skim through your calendar. It’s also hard to notice which entries are favourites, whether in calendar or normal view - favourited entries used to be highlighted in yellow so were easy to recognise, while its now just a small heart tag that is often hidden behind other tags.
